question.text: Which of the following is a correct statement?

options.text: Continuity at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></math> is sufficient for differentiability at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></math>
Differentiability at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></math> is sufficient for continuity at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></math>
Existence of limit at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></math> is sufficient for continuity at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></math>
Differentiability at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></math> is necessary for existence of tangent at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></math>

solution.text:
If fx is differentiable at x=a, then fx is also continuous at x=a
Hence, differentiability at x=a is sufficient for continuity at x=a
